title: Lanzarote or Fuerteventura: which is better for winter sun?
author: Matt
intro: They're next-door Canary Islands, half an hour apart by ferry, with the same winter warmth. The difference is what you want from the week: volcanoes and pretty villages, or long, empty beaches.
seo_title: Lanzarote or Fuerteventura? Volcanoes vs beaches
seo_description: Lanzarote for volcanoes, villages and short transfers; Fuerteventura for long, empty beaches and dunes. Weather, wind, transfers and which suits you.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Pick Lanzarote for:** volcanoes and sights
- **Pick Fuerteventura for:** long empty beaches
- **Winter highs:** about 21°C on both
- **Ferry between them:** about 30 minutes

Both islands are on UK time, both are about four hours' flight from London, and both are reliably warm when the UK isn't. Lanzarote has more to see and do; Fuerteventura has more sand. If you can't choose, you can see both on one holiday.

sections.heading: Side by side
sections.text:
| | Lanzarote | Fuerteventura |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Size | About 850 km² | About 1,660 km², twice as big |
| Best for | Volcanoes, art, villages | Beaches, dunes, watersports |
| Typical winter high | 21 to 22°C | 20 to 21°C |
| Main resorts | Puerto del Carmen, Playa Blanca, Costa Teguise | Corralejo, Caleta de Fuste, Costa Calma, Jandía |
| Feel | Tidy, white villages, lots of sights | Wild, open and quieter |

The temperatures come from the climate figures in our [Lanzarote](/destinations/lanzarote) and [Fuerteventura](/destinations/fuerteventura) guides. In practice there's very little difference: you'll be in shorts on either island from November to March, though evenings can need a jumper.

sections.heading: Why choose Lanzarote
sections.text:
Lanzarote is the island to pick if you'll get bored lying on a beach all week. Its landscape is like nowhere else in Europe: black lava fields, red volcanic cones and vineyards growing in hollows in the ash.

- **Timanfaya National Park:** a coach tour through the volcanoes, where guides show how hot the ground still is just below the surface.
- **César Manrique's work:** the artist shaped the whole island, from the lava cave of Jameos del Agua to his own house built into volcanic bubbles.
- **Papagayo beaches:** sheltered golden coves in the far south, the island's best beaches.

Local knowledge: Lanzarote has no high-rise hotels in most of the island, thanks to Manrique's campaigning in the 1970s and 80s, which is why its villages still look so white and low.

sections.heading: Why choose Fuerteventura
sections.text:
Fuerteventura has some of the longest and emptiest beaches in Europe. It's the oldest of the Canary Islands, so its volcanoes have worn down into rolling hills and the coast is lined with sand.

- **Corralejo Dunes:** a natural park of white sand dunes running down to turquoise water.
- **Sotavento:** a huge tidal lagoon on the south coast, popular with windsurfers and kitesurfers.
- **Cofete:** a wild, remote beach on the west coast, reached by a rough track.

It's quieter than Lanzarote, and the resorts are further apart. If your idea of a holiday is a long walk on a near-empty beach and a good book, it's hard to beat.

sections.heading: Wind, transfers and other differences
sections.text:
Both islands are windy, because the trade winds blow across them most of the year. Fuerteventura, whose name is sometimes read as "strong wind", gets it worst, especially in summer.

Watch out: in winter, some beaches on both islands are too exposed for a relaxing day. Look for a hotel near a sheltered bay, like Papagayo on Lanzarote or the lagoon beaches around Costa Calma on Fuerteventura.

Transfers are another real difference. Lanzarote is small, so the main resorts are 15 to 40 minutes from the airport. On Fuerteventura, Corralejo and Caleta de Fuste are close, but Jandía in the far south is over an hour away by road. Lanzarote also has more choice of restaurants and things to do in the evening, while Fuerteventura is better for space and quiet.

sections.heading: Or do both
sections.text:
You don't have to choose. Ferries run from Playa Blanca in the south of Lanzarote to Corralejo in the north of Fuerteventura many times a day, and the crossing takes about half an hour.

- **Day trip:** easy in either direction, on foot or with a car.
- **Twin-centre week:** four nights in Lanzarote for the sights and three in Corralejo for the beaches, flying into one island and out of the other if the times work.
- **Hire cars:** check the rental company's rules on taking one across on the ferry before you book.

sections.heading: Still deciding?
sections.text:
If neither feels quite right, [Gran Canaria and Tenerife](/blog/gran-canaria-or-tenerife) are bigger, with more mountains and more variety. [Madeira](/destinations/madeira) is greener and better for walking, and our guide to [winter sun with no jet lag](/blog/winter-sun-with-no-jet-lag) compares them all.

For more ideas, see the [December](/destinations/where-to-go-in-december) and [January](/destinations/where-to-go-in-january) pages. If half of you want Lanzarote and half want Fuerteventura, put both in the draw and let it decide, or read [how to choose between two holidays](/blog/how-to-choose-between-two-holidays).

faqs.question: Is Lanzarote or Fuerteventura warmer in winter?
faqs.answer: There's very little in it. Both have highs of about 20 to 22°C from December to February, with Lanzarote typically a degree warmer.

faqs.question: Which is windier, Lanzarote or Fuerteventura?
faqs.answer: Fuerteventura is generally windier, especially in summer, which is why it's so popular for windsurfing and kitesurfing. Both islands have sheltered beaches.

faqs.question: Can you get from Lanzarote to Fuerteventura by ferry?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ferries run from Playa Blanca on Lanzarote to Corralejo on Fuerteventura many times a day, and the crossing takes about 30 minutes.

faqs.question: Which has better beaches, Lanzarote or Fuerteventura?
faqs.answer: Fuerteventura, for long sandy beaches and dunes. Lanzarote's best beaches are the smaller, sheltered Papagayo coves in the south.
